simple.meaning: שָׁבוּעַ (shâbûwaʻ) is a Hebrew object word meaning “literally, sevened , i.e. a week (specifically, of years).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 29:27. The surrounding context includes family line, offering, blood.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׁבוּעַ (H7620) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: שָׁבוּעַ (shâbûwaʻ) / H7620 is traced through Genesis 29:27, Genesis 29:28, Exodus 34:22, Leviticus 12:5 with generated occurrence evidence.

timeline.evidenceText: Fulfill the week of this one, and we will give you the other also for the service which you will serve with me for seven more years.”

“You shall observe the feast of weeks with the first fruits of wheat harvest, and the feast of harvest at the year’s end.
But if she bears a female child, then she shall be unclean two weeks, as in her period; and she shall continue in the blood of purification sixty-six days.
“ ‘Also in the day of the first fruits, when you offer a new meal offering to Yahweh in your feast of weeks, you shall have a holy convocation. You shall do no regular work;
You shall count for yourselves seven weeks. From the time you begin to put the sickle to the standing grain you shall begin to count seven weeks.
You shall count for yourselves seven weeks. From the time you begin to put the sickle to the standing grain you shall begin to count seven weeks.
You shall keep the feast of weeks to Yahweh your God with a tribute of a free will offering of your hand, which you shall give according to how Yahweh your God blesses you.

Three times in a year all of your males shall appear before Yahweh your God in the place which he chooses: in the feast of unleavened bread, in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of booths. They shall not appear before Yahweh empty.

They don’t say in their heart, ‘Let’s now fear Yahweh our God, who gives rain, both the former and the latter, in its season, who preserves to us the appointed weeks of the harvest.’
“ ‘ “In the first month, in the fourteenth day of the month, you shall have the Passover, a feast of seven days; unleavened bread shall be eaten.

“Seventy weeks are decreed on your people and on your holy city, to finish disobedience, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most holy.

“Know therefore and discern that from the going out of the commandment to restore and to build Jerusalem to the Anointed One,† “Anointed One” can also be translated “Messiah” (same as “Christ”). the prince, will be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks. It will be built again, with street and moat, even in troubled times.

“Know therefore and discern that from the going out of the commandment to restore and to build Jerusalem to the Anointed One,† “Anointed One” can also be translated “Messiah” (same as “Christ”). the prince, will be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks. It will be built again, with street and moat, even in troubled times.

After the sixty-two weeks the Anointed One‡ “Anointed One” can also be translated “Messiah” (same as “Christ”). will be cut off, and will have nothing. The people of the prince who come will destroy the city and the sanctuary. Its end will be with a flood, and war will be even to the end. Desolations are determined.

He will make a firm covenant with many for one week. In the middle of the week he will cause the sacrifice and the offering to cease. On the wing of abominations will come one who makes desolate; and even to the full end, and that determined, wrath will be poured out on the desolate.”

He will make a firm covenant with many for one week. In the middle of the week he will cause the sacrifice and the offering to cease. On the wing of abominations will come one who makes desolate; and even to the full end, and that determined, wrath will be poured out on the desolate.”
In those days I, Daniel, was mourning three whole weeks.
I ate no pleasant bread. No meat or wine came into my mouth. I didn’t anoint myself at all, until three whole weeks were fulfilled.

definitions.full: H7620. shabua שָׁבוּעַ noun masculine Dan 9:27 period of seven (days, years), heptad, week (on formation see Lag BN 67 ); — absolute ׳שׁ 9:27 (twice in verse); construct שְׁבֻעַ Gen 29:27-28 , dual שְׁבֻעַיִם Lev 12:5 ; plural שָֽׁבֻע(וֺ)ת Exod 34:22 4 t. Deuteronomy + (in technical term) 2Chr 8:13 ; late שָֽׁבֻעִים Dan 9:24 4 t. Daniel; construct שְׁבֻעֹת Jer 5:24 ( Ezek 45:21 read שִׁבְעַת with Vrss and all modern, see שֶׁבַע ); suffix שָׁבֻעֹתֵיבֶם Num 28:26 ; — 1 period of seven days (froma given time), week: Deut 16:9 (twice in verse); Lev 12:5 (P); of marriage feast Gen 29:27-28 , (E; compare Judg 14:12 ; Tob 11:19); יָמִים שָׁבֻעִים Dan 10:2-3 ,three weeks, days (three weeks long); ׳שׁ קָצִיר חֻקּוֺת Jer 5:24 weeks of statutes (i.e. weeks appointed by ׳י ) for harvest ; technical term שָֽׁבֻעֹת חַגּ Exod 34:22 (J) feast of weeks (ending seven weeks of harvest), Deut 16:10 , 16 ; 2Chr 8:13 so ׳שׁ alone Num 28:26 (P). 2 heptad or seven of years, late , Dan 9:24-25 , 26 , 27 (twice in verse). — שֻׁבֻעוֺת Ezek 21:28 see שָׁבַע ].
